page.overview:
What is Pokémon Anime?

Pokémon the Series, PS, known as in Japan and in South Korea, PM, or simply Pokémon, is an ongoing animated show that originally followed the adventures of the series' main protagonist, Ash Ketchum, and his friends (Ash's Pikachu). Currently, it focuses on the adventures of Liko and Roy and the Rising Volt Tacklers in . The series is a Japanese production created under OLM, Inc. Inc. (formerly Oriental Light & Magic Inc.).

It premiered on TV Tokyo in Japan on , and it later was dubbed in English in North America on September 8, 1998 and international television by 4Kids Entertainment (until Season 8; the English dub transferred to Pokémon USA, now TPCi, from Season 9). It exists in two dubbing pipelines: the direct-from-Japanese "East Asian" pipeline followed by Korea, Greater China, Thailand, and occasionally Indonesia and Vietnam, and the English-derived "international" pipeline followed by every location outside of Asia (where the distribution rights are held by TPCi) as well as South Asia, the Middle East, and parts of Southeast Asia (where the rights are held by TPC).

It is divided into multiple "series", shows that correspond to that product line, usually a generation of the Pokémon games and media. Exclusive to the English and English-derived international pipelines are seasons, which are divided and aired according to the English opening of each episode (with the exception of Seasons 1 through 6, which were divided and aired by 52 episode segments). As of Pokémon Horizons: The Series, seasons exist in each non-Korean foreign dub of the series, including direct-from-Japanese dubs such as Thai, Mandarin, and Cantonese.

In the primary organization used by Japan and the rest of Asia (TPC-controlled regions), both the eras of Ash and Liko being the main protagonist are part of one continuous anime, with the Asian version of the English dub counting from "season 26". However, Pokémon.com and TPCi-controlled distribution retcons Pokémon Horizons: The Series into a separate anime, restarting the dub season count from "1" for marketing purposes.
